Amos 7:1.text: The Lord showed me this: Look, a brood of locusts was coming at dawn, and look, one bruchus locust, Gog the king.

Amos 7:2.text: When it finishes devouring the land’s grass, I said, “Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!

Amos 7:3.text: Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This will not happen,” says the Lord.

Amos 7:4.text: The Lord showed me this: Look, the Lord called for judgment by fire; it devoured the great abyss and devoured the portion.

Amos 7:5.text: I said, “Lord, Lord, cease, please! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!

Amos 7:6.text: Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This certainly will not happen,” says the Lord.

Amos 7:7.text: The Lord showed me this: Look, a man was standing upon an adamant wall, with adamant in his hand.

Amos 7:8.text: The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “Adamant.” The Lord said to me, “Look, I am setting adamant in the midst of My people Israel. I will certainly no longer pass them by,

Amos 7:9.text: and the altars of laughter will disappear, and Israel’s rites will be laid waste. I will rise against Jeroboam’s house with a sword.”

Amos 7:10.text: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos is forming conspiracies against you in the midst of Israel’s house. The land certainly cannot endure all his words,

Amos 7:11.text: because Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by a sword, and Israel will be led captive away from its land.’”

Amos 7:12.text: Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, go! Withdraw to Judah’s land; make your living there, and there you will prophesy.

Amos 7:13.text: But you must never again prophesy at Bethel, because it is a king’s sanctuary and a house of kingship.”

Amos 7:14.text: Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,

Amos 7:15.text: and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’

Amos 7:16.text: Now hear the Lord’s word: You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and you must not stir up a crowd against Jacob’s house.’

Amos 7:17.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: ‘Your wife will practice prostitution in the city, your sons and daughters will fall by a sword, and your land will be measured out with a cord. You will die in an unclean land, and Israel will be led captive away from its land.’”

Amos 8:1.text: The Lord showed me this: Look, a fowler’s vessel.

Amos 8:2.text: He said, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A fowler’s vessel.” The Lord said to me, “The end has arrived upon My people Israel. I will certainly no longer pass them by.

Amos 8:3.text: The temple’s coffered ceilings will wail. On that day,” says the Lord, “many have fallen in every place. I will cast silence upon them.”

Amos 8:4.text: Hear these things now, you who wear out the needy until morning and oppress the poor out of the land,

Amos 8:5.text: saying, “When will the month pass, so we may trade, and the sabbaths, so we may open storehouses, making the measure small and the weights great and making an unjust balance,

Amos 8:6.text: to acquire the poor with silver and a lowly person in exchange for sandals? And we will trade from every kind of produce.”

Amos 8:7.text: The Lord swears by Jacob’s arrogance: “He will never forget all your works.”

Amos 8:8.text: Will the earth not be disturbed over these things, and everyone dwelling in it mourn? A consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.

Amos 8:9.text: “On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at midday, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime.

Amos 8:10.text: I will turn your festivals to mourning and all your songs to lamentation. I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head; I will make him like mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain.

Amos 8:11.text: Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will send famine upon the earth: not famine for bread or thirst for water, but famine for hearing the Lord’s word.

Amos 8:12.text: Waters will be shaken as far as the sea, and from north to east they will run about seeking the Lord’s word, but certainly will not find it.

Amos 8:13.text: On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst,

Amos 8:14.text: those who swear by Samaria’s propitiation and say, ‘Your god lives, Dan!’ and ‘Your god lives, Beersheba!’ They will fall and certainly never rise again.”

Joel 1:4.text: What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.

Joel 1:5.text: Sober up, you drunkards, from their wine, and weep! Lament, all who drink wine to intoxication, because gladness and joy have been removed from your mouths.

Joel 1:6.text: For a nation has come up against My land, strong and uncountable. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth, and its grinding teeth a young lion’s.

Joel 1:7.text: It laid My vine waste and shattered My fig trees; searching, it searched it out and cast it away; it whitened its branches.

Joel 2:12.text: “And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”

Joel 2:13.text: Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.

Joel 2:14.text: Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?

Joel 2:15.text: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.

Joel 2:16.text: Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.

Joel 2:17.text: In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”

Joel 2:18.text: Then the Lord became jealous for His land and spared His people.

Exodus 32:7.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Go quickly from here and come down, for your people, whom you led out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.

Exodus 32:8.text: They have quickly transgressed the way you commanded them. They have made themselves a calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.’

Exodus 32:10.text: Now leave Me alone, and in the heat of My wrath against them I will destroy them. I will make you into a great nation.”

Exodus 32:11.text: Moses entreated the Lord God and said, “Why, O Lord, art Thou angry with Thy people, whom Thou didst lead out of the land of Egypt with great strength and Thine uplifted arm?

Exodus 32:12.text: Let not the Egyptians say, ‘He led them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth.’ Cease from Thy fierce anger and be merciful concerning Thy people’s evil,

Exodus 32:13.text: remembering Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thyself and speak, saying, ‘I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude’; and all this land which Thou didst say Thou wouldest give to their seed, they shall possess for ever.”

Exodus 32:14.text: The Lord was appeased concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon His people.

Deuteronomy 32:19.text: And the Lord saw, and was jealous, and was provoked by the anger of His sons and daughters.

Deuteronomy 32:20.text: And He said, I will turn My face from them, and show what shall befall them at the last; for they are a perverse generation, sons in whom is no faithfulness.

Deuteronomy 32:21.text: They made Me jealous with that which is no god; they provoked Me to anger with their idols. And I will make them jealous with that which is no nation; with a nation without understanding will I provoke them to anger.

Deuteronomy 32:22.text: For a fire has been kindled out of My wrath; it shall burn unto Hades beneath, devour the earth and its produce, and set ablaze the foundations of the mountains.

Deuteronomy 32:23.text: I will gather evils against them, and spend My arrows upon them.

Deuteronomy 32:24.text: They shall waste away with hunger, and be devoured by birds, and suffer incurable backward-bending spasms; I will send against them the teeth of wild beasts, with the fury of things that crawl upon the ground.

Hosea 10:5.text: Samaria’s inhabitants will dwell beside the calf of the house of On, because its people mourned over it; just as they embittered it, they will rejoice over its glory, because it was deported from it.

Hosea 10:6.text: They bound it and carried it to the Assyrians as guest-gifts for King Jarim. He will receive Ephraim as a gift, and Israel will be ashamed of his counsel.

Hosea 10:7.text: Samaria cast off her king like a twig on the water’s surface.

Hosea 10:8.text: The shrines of On, Israel’s sins, will be removed; thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us!’ and to the hills, ‘Fall upon us!’

Jeremiah 33:8.text: And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!

Jeremiah 33:9.text: Because you prophesied in the Lord’s name, saying, This house will be like Shiloh and this city will be emptied of inhabitants. And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord’s house.

Jeremiah 33:10.text: And Judah’s rulers heard this word and went up from the king’s house to the Lord’s house. They sat before the Lord’s New Gate.

Jeremiah 33:11.text: And the priests and false prophets said to the rulers and all the people: A sentence of death for this man, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears!

Acts 4:13.text: When they observed Peter’s and John’s boldness and realized that they were unlettered, ordinary men, they were amazed. They also recognized that they had been with Jesus.

Acts 4:14.text: Seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.

Acts 4:15.text: They ordered them to leave the council and conferred with one another,

Acts 4:16.text: saying, “What should we do with these men? That a notable sign has taken place through them is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.

Acts 4:17.text: But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them with threats not to speak to anyone in this name again.”

Acts 4:18.text: They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.

Acts 4:19.text: Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;

Acts 4:20.text: for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

Luke 13:31.text: At that very hour some Pharisees approached and said to Him, “Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill Thee.”

Luke 13:32.text: And He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I drive out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion.’

Luke 13:33.text: Nevertheless, I must travel today and tomorrow and the day following, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.

Zechariah 13:1.text: On that day every place will be opened in David’s house.

Zechariah 13:2.text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the idols’ names from the land, and there will no longer be remembrance of them. I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

Zechariah 13:3.text: If a person still prophesies, his father and mother who begot him will say to him, ‘You shall not live, because you spoke falsehoods in the Lord’s name.’ His father and mother who begot him will bind his feet when he prophesies.

Zechariah 13:4.text: On that day the prophets will be ashamed, each because of his vision when he prophesies; they will wear a hairy skin because they lied.

Zechariah 13:5.text: He will say, ‘I am no prophet; I am a man who works the earth, because a man begot me from my youth.’

Zechariah 13:6.text: I will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your hands?’ He will say, ‘The ones with which I was struck in my beloved house.’

2 Samuel 7:4.text: That night a word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,

2 Samuel 7:5.text: “Go and say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the Lord: You will not build Me a house for Me to dwell in,

2 Samuel 7:6.text: for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt until this day. I have been moving about in a lodging and a tent.

2 Samuel 7:7.text: Wherever I passed through among all Israel, did I ever speak to one of Israel’s tribes whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, “Why have you not built Me a cedar house?”

2 Samuel 7:8.text: Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people, over Israel,

2 Samuel 7:9.text: and I was with you wherever you went and destroyed all your enemies before you, and I made you renowned, according to the name of the great ones on the earth.

Isaiah 30:8.text: Now then, sit and write these things on a tablet and in a book, because these things will endure for days of appointed times and for ever.

Isaiah 30:9.text: For this is a disobedient people, lying sons who did not want to hear God’s law,

Isaiah 30:10.text: who say to the prophets, “Do not announce to us,” and to those seeing visions, “Do not speak to us. Instead, speak to us and announce another deception,

Isaiah 30:11.text: and turn us from this way, remove this path from us, and remove Israel’s Holy One from us.”

Jeremiah 20:1.text: And Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who had been appointed leader of the Lord’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.

Jeremiah 20:2.text: And he struck him and put him into the trap, which was at the gate of the separated upper house that was in the Lord’s house.

Jeremiah 20:3.text: And Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the trap, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has called your name not Pashhur but Migrant.

Jeremiah 20:4.text: Because thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving you to migration with all your friends. They will fall by their enemies’ sword, and your eyes will see. I will give you and all Judah into the hands of Babylon’s king, and they will deport them and cut them down with swords.

Jeremiah 20:5.text: And I will give all this city’s strength, all its labors, and all the treasures of Judah’s king into his enemies’ hands, and they will bring them to Babylon.

Jeremiah 20:6.text: And you and all who dwell in your house will go into captivity. In Babylon you will die and there be buried—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied false things.

Ezekiel 38:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 38:2.text: “Son of man, set your face firmly against Gog and the land of Magog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel, and prophesy against him,

Ezekiel 38:3.text: and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,

Ezekiel 38:4.text: and I will gather you and all your force, horses and horsemen all clothed in breastplates, a great assembly, small shields, helmets and swords,

Ezekiel 3:8.text: Behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your contention against their contention,

Ezekiel 3:9.text: and it will always be stronger than rock. Do not fear them or be terrified before their faces, for it is an embittering house.”

Ezekiel 7:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 7:2.text: “And you, son of man, say, ‘Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel: An end has come; the end has come upon the four wings of the land.

Ezekiel 7:4.text: upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day has drawn near, neither with tumult nor with birth pangs.

Proverbs 22:22.text: Do not use force against the needy, for he is poor, and do not dishonor the weak at the gates;

Proverbs 22:23.text: for the Lord will judge his case, and you will preserve your own life unplundered.

Deuteronomy 25:13.text: You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.

Deuteronomy 25:14.text: You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.

Deuteronomy 25:15.text: You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.

Deuteronomy 25:16.text: For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is an abomination unto the Lord your God.

Amos 2:6.text: Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sold a righteous person for silver and a poor person for sandals,

Amos 2:7.text: which tread upon the earth’s dust. They struck the heads of the poor with their fists and turned aside the way of the humble; a son and his father went in to the same young slave woman, to profane the name of their God,

Amos 2:8.text: and, tying their garments with cords, they made hangings next to the altar, and drank wine from extortions in their God’s house.

Hosea 7:1.text: when I heal Israel. Ephraim’s injustice and Samaria’s wickedness will be uncovered, because they practiced falsehood. A thief will enter upon him, a robber stripping him on his road,

Hosea 7:2.text: so that they sing together as people singing together with their heart. I remembered all their evils; now their schemes have surrounded them; they have come before My face.

Hosea 7:3.text: With their evils they gladdened kings, and with their falsehoods, rulers.

Amos 9:5.text: The Lord, Lord God Almighty, touches the earth and shakes it; all who dwell in it will mourn. Its consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.

Amos 9:6.text: He builds His ascent into heaven and establishes His promise upon the earth; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name.

Jeremiah 15:9.text: She who bore seven was emptied; her soul grew faint. Her sun set while the day was still at its middle; she was ashamed and reproached. Their remnants I will give to the sword before their enemies.

Jeremiah 6:24.text: We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.

Jeremiah 6:25.text: Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.

Jeremiah 6:26.text: Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.

Ezekiel 7:16.text: Their survivors will be saved and be on the mountains; I will kill them all, each in his injustices.

Ezekiel 7:17.text: All hands will weaken, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture,

Ezekiel 7:18.text: and they will gird on sackcloth; amazement will cover them, shame will be upon every face among them, and baldness upon every head.

1 Samuel 3:1.text: The child Samuel ministered to the Lord before Eli the priest. The Lord’s word was precious in those days; there was no distinct vision.

1 Samuel 3:2.text: At that time Eli was sleeping in his place. His eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see,

1 Samuel 3:3.text: and it was before God’s lamp was put in order. Samuel was sleeping in the sanctuary where God’s ark was,

1 Samuel 3:4.text: and the Lord called, “Samuel, Samuel!” He said, “Here I am.”

Deuteronomy 8:1.text: All the commandments which I command you this day you shall take heed to do, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God sware unto your fathers.

Deuteronomy 8:2.text: And you shall remember all the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, to afflict you and to test you, that the things in your heart might be known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.

Deuteronomy 8:3.text: And He afflicted you, and made you hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers did not know, that He might declare unto you that man shall not live by bread alone, but man shall live by every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.

1 Samuel 28:3.text: Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him at Armathaim, in his city. Saul had removed the mediums and the knowers from the land.

1 Samuel 28:4.text: The foreigners gathered, came, and camped at Soman. Saul gathered every man of Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.

1 Samuel 28:5.text: Saul saw the foreigners’ camp and was afraid, and his heart was greatly astounded.

1 Samuel 28:6.text: Saul inquired through the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him by dreams, by clear signs, or by prophets.

1 Samuel 28:7.text: Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so that I may go to her and inquire through her.” His servants said to him, “There is a woman who is a medium at Endor.”

Lamentations 4:1.text: How the gold will grow dim, how the good silver will change! Holy stones were poured out at the head of every way out.

Lamentations 4:2.text: Zion’s precious sons, exalted in gold— how they were regarded as earthen vessels, works of a potter’s hands!

Lamentations 4:3.text: Even dragons bared breasts, and their young suckled; the daughters of my people have become incurable, like a sparrow in the wilderness.

Lamentations 4:4.text: The nursing child’s tongue clung to its throat with thirst. Infants asked for bread; there is no one to break it for them.

Lamentations 4:5.text: Those who ate luxuries were destroyed at the ways out; those nursed upon scarlet wrapped themselves in dung heaps.

Lamentations 4:6.text: The lawlessness of the daughter of my people became greater than Sodom’s lawlessness, which was overthrown as in haste, and they did not labor their hands upon it.

1 Kings 12:26.text: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Behold, now the kingdom will return to David’s house.

1 Kings 12:27.text: If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the Lord’s house in Jerusalem, the people’s heart will return to the Lord and their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me.”

1 Kings 12:29.text: He placed one in Bethel and put the other in Dan.

1 Kings 12:30.text: This matter became a sin. The people went before the one as far as Dan.

1 Kings 12:33.text: He went up onto the altar he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, at the feast he had fashioned from his heart. He held a feast for the sons of Israel and went up onto the altar to offer sacrifice.

Hosea 1:2.text: The beginning of the Lord’s word to Hosea. The Lord said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a woman of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land will utterly prostitute itself away from following the Lord.”

Hosea 6:6.text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.
